svg.title: Figure 1 · The exported scenes
svg.desc: Every exported scene with its kind, hazards, outcome, frames, freshness and the pages that replay it
svg.text: 6 exports, one per scene, written by export_scene.py from each scene's motion block and the records it names; 6 of 6 match a fresh export. Every page of a scene and its look
Slow supply leak on a slope; balance lost before the hold …
Protective stop removes leg force instead of crouching
Frozen posture feedback with no staleness monitor
Burst supply loss with failed load holding; the cockpit drops
Link loss with return-to-launch; the UAV descends into the …
Link loss after the walker moved; the UAV lands at the …

Walker exports carry a performed run (the fault as it happens) and an intended run (what should happen) from sim/plant/walker.py; UAV exports carry one PX4 SITL run from sim/results/uav/. The SUS-M1 sheet replays the
Generated by tools/figures/sceneout_readme.py from the exported scene analysis and the code that writes and reads it. Synthetic, design aid only, no evidence credit (sim/README.md, evidence gate).

g.text: Terms: 3D = three-dimensional · EC-nnn = edge case found by a failure search · FLT-nnn = walker fault in sim/faults.yaml · HAZ-nnn = hazard record (safety/hazards/HAZ-xxx-nnn.yaml) · KB = kilobyte, a file size of
1,024 bytes · PX4 = PX4 Autopilot, the open-source flight-control software candidate for SUS-A1 · S3-nnn = 3D hazard scene (sim/scenes3d) · SF-nnn = walker failure-search family (sim/search) · SITL =
software-in-the-loop simulation · SU-nnn = UAV PX4 SITL scenario · SUS-A1 = dockable observation UAV · SUS-M1 = piloted walker · UAV = uncrewed aerial vehicle (drone)
